exchanges.author: c_leilani
exchanges.body: trying to run the tests for your #1494 on my laptop to learn the DST stuff and I get ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key America/Chicago'. did I break something? (Windows, Python 3.12 from python.org)

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: You didn't break anything! Windows has no IANA time zone database, so zoneinfo can't find America/Chicago unless the tzdata package is installed: `pip install tzdata` in your venv (it's the first-party package the zoneinfo docs recommend). Our ECS images are Linux with system tzdata, so production is fine. Then run `python3 -m unittest` on the #1494 branch: all should pass, and on main 3 of the 4 new DST tests fail, which is the point.

exchanges.author: c_priya
exchanges.subject: PG17 upgrade: Billing's checklist (reply by Tue 17:00)
exchanges.body: Hi Jordan, Nadia said you're Billing's point for the Postgres 17 upgrade. Checklist attached; item 1 is the one that bites teams: functions used in expression indexes that reference anything unqualified. If you find one, the fix has to be a migration merged before Wednesday 18:00. pg17-staging has a fresh copy of billing-db from Friday. Happy to jump on a call. Priya

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body:
Priya, Billing's answers:
1. One hit. The reminders_local_day expression index (migration 0031) uses reminder_local_day(timestamptz, text), which calls canonical_tz(text) unqualified, which reads tz_aliases unqualified. Under PG17's safe search_path (pg_catalog, pg_temp) your post-upgrade ANALYZE fails on reminders (we reproduced it on pg17-staging: 'function canonical_tz(text) does not exist'), and so would any REINDEX. Fix: migration 0043 sets search_path = public, pg_temp on both functions; PR #1495, merging before Wednesday 18:00. No other expression indexes or materialized views in billing-db.
2. Extensions: confirmed pg_stat_statements and pgcrypto only.
3. old_snapshot_threshold: default, nothing to do.
4. Test suite against pg17-staging: tomorrow, I'll post results.
5. Saturday owner: me (Jordan), phone in PagerDuty.

exchanges.author: c_aisha
exchanges.subject: Review requested: #1490
exchanges.body:
Adds billing/proration.py and tests for the cancellation credit. Could you review?

```diff
+++ billing/proration.py
+"""Credit for a mid-period cancellation."""
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
+
+
+def prorated_credit(price: str, period_start: date, period_end: date, cancel_on: date) -> Decimal:
+    days = (period_end - period_start).days + 1
+    remaining = (period_end - cancel_on).days
+    return (Decimal(price) * remaining / days).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ROUND_HALF_UP)
+++ tests/test_proration.py
+    def test_mid_month(self):
+        self.assertEqual(prorated_credit("499.00", date(2026, 11, 1), date(2026, 11, 30), date(2026, 11, 18)),
+                         Decimal("199.60"))
+
+    def test_cancel_on_first_day(self):
+        self.assertEqual(prorated_credit("300.00", date(2026, 11, 1), date(2026, 11, 30), date(2026, 11, 1)),
+                         Decimal("290.00"))
```

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body:
Nice, small and readable, Leilani. One real issue, and it's the classic money one: float. round() works on binary approximations and rounds ties to even, so half-cent lines come out a cent low. With your code, 2.5 h x 19.99 = 49.975 gives 49.97 (should be 49.98), and 1.25 h x 130.10 = 162.625 gives 162.62 (should be 162.63). A 10% discount on 24.45 gives 2.44 (should be 2.45).

docs/money.md has the rule: Decimal built from strings, quantize each line to the cent with ROUND_HALF_UP, sum the rounded lines, discount on the subtotal also half up. proration.py in #1490 uses the same pattern. Your tests pass because none of them has a half cent; add those three cases (they fail on this branch). Want to pair on it tomorrow?

threads.title: PR #1492 Webhook retry policy with backoff and jitter (Ben)

exchanges.author: c_ben
exchanges.subject: Review requested: #1492
exchanges.body:
BIL-1480: the retry policy the delivery task will call. Capped exponential backoff with full jitter, 8 attempts max.

```diff
+++ billing/retry.py
+BASE_S = 30              # first retry within 30 s, doubling each attempt
+CAP_S = 6 * 3600         # never wait more than 6 hours
+MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8
+
+def should_retry(status: int | None, attempt: int) -> bool:
+    """status is None when there was no response (timeout, connection error)."""
+    if attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+        return False
+    return status is None or status >= 400
+
+def next_delay(attempt: int, rng: random.Random = random) -> float:
+    return rng.uniform(0, min(CAP_S, BASE_S * 2 ** attempt))
+++ tests/test_retry.py
+    (retries 500 and None, not 200, stops at MAX_ATTEMPTS, delay capped)
```
CI green. Wiring it into the delivery task is a follow-up.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body:
Thanks Ben, the capped backoff with full jitter looks right. Two things before it merges:

1. should_retry retries every status >= 400, so an endpoint that answers 400, 401, 404 or 410 Gone gets all 8 attempts, about 2 hours of backoff. Those mean the request was refused and won't change on repeat (410 literally says the resource won't come back). Retry only no-response, 408, 429 and 5xx.
2. 429 and 503 often carry Retry-After (delay-seconds or an HTTP-date, RFC 9110). Honor it, capped at CAP_S, instead of our own backoff, or we keep hitting a tenant that's asked us to wait.

Tests: 400/401/404/410/422 as no-retry, and a Retry-After case for each form. Nit: with attempt starting at 1 the first wait is up to 60 s, not 30 as the comment says.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body:
PR #1495 Pin search_path on the reminders_local_day index functions (PG17)

Migration 0043: ALTER FUNCTION ... SET search_path = public, pg_temp on canonical_tz(text) and reminder_local_day(timestamptz, text), the two functions behind the reminders_local_day expression index (0031). Under PG17's safe search_path, ANALYZE reminders on pg17-staging fails with 'function canonical_tz(text) does not exist'; with 0043 applied it succeeds (checked with Priya). documents.title: RFC-031: Transactional outbox relay for invoice side effects (Marcus)

versions.author: c_marcus
versions.content:
# RFC-031: Transactional outbox relay for invoice side effects

Status: open for comment until Wed 11/4. Author: Marcus Lee.

Problem. finalize_invoice sends webhooks and the invoice email from inside a Celery task. If the task fails
after the invoice commits, side effects are lost; if it's redelivered, they can repeat (INV-2240).

Proposal. finalize_invoice writes the invoice and its outbound_events rows in one database transaction and
sends nothing. A relay process polls `SELECT * FROM outbound_events WHERE sent_at IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 100`
every second, sends each event, and sets sent_at. This makes delivery exactly-once: each row is sent once and
then marked sent.

Rollout. One relay in Sprint 46; scale to three relays for throughput in Sprint 47.

Open questions. Polling interval; what to alert on.

"""Webhook signatures (BIL-1476): every delivery carries
Tallyfin-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with the endpoint's signing secret>.
"""
import hashlib
import hmac
import json


def signature_header(secret: str, payload: dict, timestamp: int) -> str:
    body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    mac = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{timestamp}.{body}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return f"t={timestamp},v1={mac}"

import unittest
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone

from billing.reminders import send_time_utc


class TestReminderDST(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_scheduled_before_us_fall_back(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

                         datetime(2026, 10, 26, 9, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_scheduled_before_sydney_spring_forward(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 2, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(send_time_utc(date(2026, 10, 5), "Australia/Sydney", now),
                         datetime(2026, 10, 4, 22, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_phoenix_no_dst(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(send_time_utc(date(2026, 11, 2), "America/Phoenix", now),
                         datetime(2026, 11, 2, 16, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
"""PG17 safe search_path (Platform's PG17 checklist, item 1).

The reminders_local_day expression index (0031) calls reminder_local_day(), which calls canonical_tz() unqualified,
which reads tz_aliases unqualified. PG17 runs ANALYZE, REINDEX, VACUUM and CREATE INDEX with search_path =
pg_catalog, pg_temp, so both lookups fail there. Pin each function's search path; no table is touched.
"""
from alembic import op

revision = "0043"
down_revision = "0041"


def upgrade():
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.canonical_tz(text) SET search_path = public, pg_temp")
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.reminder_local_day(timestamptz, text) SET search_path = public, pg_temp")


def downgrade():
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.reminder_local_day(timestamptz, text) RESET search_path")
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.canonical_tz(text) RESET search_path")
